October 9, 2014 through April 6, 2015.

statutory.question: Does the conduct described fall within 5324?
statutory.answer: Insufficient facts to determine whether 31 U.S.C. § 5324 applies (i.e., whether § 5324 prohibits structuring here).
statutory.label: neutral
statutory.reasoning: 31 U.S.C. § 5324 prohibits structuring (and related conduct) done “for the purpose of evading” Bank Secrecy Act reporting requirements (e.g., causing or attempting to cause a financial institution to fail to file a required report, or structuring/assisting in structuring transactions to evade such reporting). The fact pattern shows several large cash transactions (e.g., $86,250.37; $106,029.35; $86,730.65; $33,191.21) and one small cash deposit ($1,707.65), plus a large card transaction. However, the key statutory element under 31 U.S.C. § 5324—intent/purpose to evade a reporting requirement—is not established: there is no information that the business broke up cash deposits into amounts below a reporting threshold, directed others to do so, or otherwise acted to avoid a required report. Additionally, the listed cash amounts are not shown as being split into multiple sub-threshold transactions; several are single large cash transactions that would typically trigger reporting rather than evade it, but the record does not specify whether these are deposits/withdrawals at a financial institution, whether any CTR (or other required report) was due, or whether any report was avoided or attempted to be avoided. Because the facts do not show purposeful evasion or structuring behavior, it cannot be determined that § 5324 prohibits structuring here.
